title: Short Stuff: Calamity Jane
summary: Short Stuff episode on Calamity Jane (born Martha Jane Canary), the Old West figure. The hosts cover how little is verifiable about her given self-promoting autobiography and dime store novels; her childhood on wagon trains and the deaths of her mother and father, leaving her in charge of younger siblings at about thirteen; her work as nurse, dishwasher, scout and sharpshooter; her friendship with Wild Bill Hickok, who was murdered in Deadwood in August 1876; speculation about her sexuality, a supposed marriage to Clinton Burke and a supposed daughter, which is unverified; her drinking binges that cost her jobs with Buffalo Bill's Wild West show and the Pan American Exposition; and the disputed origin of her nickname from a story about Captain Egan at Goose Creek, Wyoming.

segments.title: Intro and historical reliability
segments.summary: Hosts introduce Calamity Jane, note how hard it is to separate fact from myth in Old West biographies, and mention her autobiography and dime store novels.

segments.title: Birth and childhood on the wagon trail
segments.summary: Born Martha Jane Canary in Princeton, Missouri, to a poor family that moved often. She learned to shoot on wagon trains, lost her mother around age nine or ten, and her father died a couple of years later, leaving her the oldest of several siblings at about thirteen.

segments.title: Early work and drinking
segments.summary: As a teen she supported her siblings by working as a nurse, dishwasher and sometimes as a sex worker, began drinking heavily, and built a reputation as a sharp shot. She later took jobs with the military as a scout, including with General Custer.

segments.title: Friendship with Wild Bill Hickok and his murder
segments.summary: Her legend grew through association with Wild Bill Hickok, with whom she was close friends in Deadwood. She was there when he was shot in the back of the head by Jack McCall in August 1876 in a Deadwood saloon, and she left town soon after.

segments.title: Sexuality and family speculation
segments.summary: The hosts discuss speculation that she was gay, a possible marriage to Clinton Burke in El Paso and a possible daughter, noting no certificates exist and a later claimed daughter was exposed as a fraud.

segments.title: Wild West shows, drinking binges and the nickname origin
segments.summary: She was a sharpshooter with Buffalo Bill's Wild West show until drinking cost her the job, and later lost a Pan American Exposition job for the same reason. The hosts then recount her own account of getting the nickname from Captain Egan at Goose Creek, Wyoming, which they consider questionable.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wrap up, praising her survival as a young girl in the West, and close the episode with the network credit.
